prompt: Review the order-service architecture decision record in docs/adr/0007-event-sourced-orders.md and the supporting packet around it. I own this change and need a decision I can take to the architecture council, not a rewrite of the design. Check whether the proposed behavior, operations, migration, and dependencies fit the contracts and targets in the packet, and call out concrete consequences where the design is incomplete or inconsistent. Keep the review focused on issues that could change approval or implementation work. Write the review to REVIEW.md at the top of the project. End it with a fenced json list of findings, each with location (the section number of the document, like 3.2), severity (critical, high, medium, low or nit), issue and fix.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const S=["critical","high","medium","low","nit"];process.exit(L.every(x=>x.location&&S.includes(String(x.severity).toLowerCase())&&(x.issue||x.fix||x.text))?0:1)'

node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const H=new Set();for(const l of fs.readFileSync("docs/adr/0007-event-sourced-orders.md","utf8").split("\n")){const m=l.match(/^#+\s*(?:section\s*)?(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)/i);if(m)H.add(m[1])}process.exit(L.every(x=>{const m=String(x.location).match(/\d+(?:\.\d+)*/);return m&&H.has(m[0])})?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: Each important finding identifies the concrete consequence in this project and gives a fix a developer can act on, without inventing problems unsupported by the packet. Fail: generic findings ('add validation', 'consider security'), or a finding the packet does not support, or neither the read-your-writes conflict (product-requirements.md against 3.3) nor the replay arithmetic (174.66 M events at 2.5 M per minute is about 70 minutes, not ten) is found. Partial: findings are grounded in the packet but some lack an actionable fix or a concrete consequence, or the review finds only gaps a reader of the ADR alone could list. Pass: both the read-your-writes conflict and the replay arithmetic are found with their numbers, every important finding names the section, the consequence in this project and a fix a developer can build, and no finding is invented. (code cannot check this because it requires judging the review's reasoning against the project context).

The review ends in a decision the owner can take to the architecture council. Fail: no verdict, or 'approve' while a critical finding is open. Partial: says 'not ready' but not what must change for approval. Pass: a clear verdict (not ready, or approve the spike only) that names the findings that must close first, at least the recovery-time and read-your-writes ones. (code cannot check this: whether a verdict follows from the findings is a judgement.)

findingsKey.finding: The design keeps immutable events for the life of the service but only promises optional fields and consumer tolerance, with no event versioning, upcaster policy, or procedure for incompatible domain changes over years of stored data.

The customer endpoints read an asynchronous projection and explicitly return stale data when it is behind, contradicting the product requirement that a successful placement is immediately visible and leaving no read-your-writes mechanism.

At 2.5 million events per minute, replaying the 174.66 million current events takes about 70 minutes rather than the stated ten, so the full rebuild cannot meet the 15-minute recovery target and the projected growth worsens it.

The proposal stores customer and delivery personal data in an indefinitely retained immutable event log but only deletes projections, so the product deletion contract has no way to erase or irreversibly de-identify the source data.

The options table compares event sourcing with an inaccurately reduced CRUD baseline and omits the existing outbox plus audit-table design, which could provide reliable integration and history with materially less migration and operational cost.
Snapshots are deferred to a later spike without specifying when they are created, how writes coordinate with them, where they are stored and indexed, or how their format and retention are operated.

Removing the reporting team's direct SQL access and pointing vaguely to an API, daily export, or future feed does not replace its current-day SQL contract, seven-year reproducibility, or full audit fields.

items.text: States that the ADR's five minutes for restore and startup (6.2) is below the packet's measured 11-minute PostgreSQL restore (recovery-targets.md), so at most about 4 minutes of the 15-minute RTO are left for any rebuild. Also counts: 'restore alone takes 11 of the 15 minutes'. Weak: 'recovery may be slow'. Do not require the replay figure; the 70-minute replay math is the seeded finding k3, not this point.

States that projections and the relay checkpoint an 'event position', but the (order_id, sequence) key gives no global, commit-ordered position, so a cursor can skip rows that commit out of order. Also counts: 'no global sequence or log position for checkpoints', 'cursor gaps under concurrent commits'. Weak: 'add monitoring for relay lag'. Do not require a named fix (logical decoding, transaction id, commit-order table).

States that partitioning order_events by event month (4.1) conflicts with the (order_id, sequence) primary key or spreads one order's stream across partitions, so uniqueness, version checks or stream reads are not bounded. Also counts: 'partition by order id or hash instead'. Weak: 'review partitioning monthly'. Do not require a specific partitioning scheme.

Says what happens when one event fails every retry: whether it stops that order's stream or the whole projection, what readers see, and what the operator does (skip, park or stop). Also counts: 'a poison event stalls the customer projection; define skip, park or stop'. Weak: 'add a dead-letter queue' with no behaviour. Do not require command throttling.

States that the ADR gives no storage, backup or rebuild cost figure against the 2,400 USD per month first-year persistence budget (recovery-targets.md), which also rejects an unbounded rebuild step. Also counts: 'no capacity plan against the stated budget'. Weak: 'consider cost'. Do not require a list of every cost line.

items.text: Names one concrete split-brain case in the flag rollout (5.1, 5.2): legacy tables written from the asynchronous projection lag behind, a retry or read is served by the other path, the command receipt lives in only one path, or rollback rebuilds legacy tables from a projection that lacks their fields. Weak: 'the migration looks reasonable'. Do not require all four cases.

States that the plan does not fit the team (team-and-oncall.md): from 22:00 to 08:00 only platform is on call and platform cannot own an order-specific replay, or no one on the rotation has run an event-store migration, or the many schema changes exceed the two-migrations-per-month change budget. Any one of the three passes. Weak: 'document the runbook' or 'train the team'.

items.text: States that the backfill cannot rebuild exact history where audit rows lack old values (the 'state capture' event is not history), so parity must be defined as current-state parity, with historical fidelity only where the data exists. Weak: 'validate the migration'. Do not require a numeric parity threshold.

items.text: States that the current relay publishes OrderPlaced, OrderCancelled and OrderUpdated (current-architecture.md) but the ADR maps only OrderPlaced to fulfillment and has no OrderUpdated event, so the fulfillment contract changes with no migration note. Also counts: 'message types drop', 'only OrderPlaced is mapped'. Weak: 'check downstream consumers'. Do not require naming both missing types.

weakAnswers: The proposal is well structured and keeping PostgreSQL makes it a practical choice.
Consider scalability, observability, and security before implementation.
The migration plan and rollback strategy look reasonable, so approve the spike.
Add monitoring for lag and a dead-letter queue.

verdicts.note: The prompt asks for a review of behavior, operations, migration, and dependencies against contracts and targets. It does not hint at specific problems, name a checklist, or give the number of issues.
The prompt clearly specifies reviewing the ADR at fixture/docs/adr/0007-event-sourced-orders.md, writing findings to REVIEW.md, and using section numbers as locations with severity levels.

Finding the issues requires cross-file reading between the ADR and multiple packet documents (product-requirements, recovery-targets, reporting-contract, current-architecture). A quick skim would miss the arithmetic error, the read-your-writes conflict, and the reporting contract gaps.

All key items are grounded in the fixture. Each section referenced in the key exists in the ADR, and the supporting documents contain the contradictory contracts. The recovery math error (k3) is verifiable arithmetic.
No comments, tests, or file names point at planted problems. The incident document mentions stale reads but as a past operational issue, not as a hint about the ADR's design flaw.

items.note: Request asks to review an ADR without prescribing a specific method or framework; no misleading hints.
Fixture contains ADR and supporting documents but does not list findings or expert key items.
FindingsKey items reference specific issues in the ADR document; rubric anchors reward grounded, actionable findings.
Competent developer can analyze ADR to identify issues; different wording or structure of findings could still pass.

adjudication: Credit the point, not the grammar: a question, a stated gap or a proposed fix all count, if the consequence is stated or obvious.
A finding placed in a neighbouring section still counts for the judge when its text names the planted problem; the hidden test accepts the section lists in key.json.
Severity one level off from the key is half credit in the hidden test; judges do not re-score severity.
e1 passes only on the 11-minute measured restore; replay arithmetic alone is the seeded finding k3, not e1.
Score points, not length: an extra correct finding never adds or subtracts; an extra finding the packet contradicts fails r1.
A review that repeats an ADR sentence without saying what breaks and for whom is Partial at most on r1.
